prompt: Production sprite sheet for GenVo, a near-vertical top-down native 32x32 pixel-art ecology game. Make ONE transparent 2 by 2 sprite sheet, four equal square cells, generous transparent gutter, no lines or labels. Each cell is one successive animation phase of the SAME small patch of burning vegetation seen from DIRECTLY ABOVE. A restrained irregular branching cluster of orange flame tongues and glowing golden ember cores seen from overhead, short curled shapes spreading radially sideways in the ground plane, a few small dark copper edge clusters. Clearly recognize real active fire at tiny game size. Flat overhead patch, NOT an upright campfire symbol, NOT side-view teardrop flames, NOT isometric, no logs, no painted ground, no smoke cloud, no ash disk, no burned plants or debris, no environmental objects, no text or UI badge. Use transparent negative-space gaps so actual ground and creatures stay visible. Four phases change the curl and brightness of the same coherent patch with roughly equal footprint, not four separate designs. Crisp chunky hand-composed pixel clusters, no gradients, blur, glow bloom, antialiasing, photographic detail or stipple noise. Limited palette around dark copper #843b29, burnt orange #bd5429, orange #e47b32, gold #f6ad48, pale hot core #ffdc85. Keep each patch centered and entirely within its cell; its shape occupies about 65 percent of the cell width and height, irregular and sparse. The four phases will be mechanically nearest-sampled to 32x32 each.
